prediction.raw:

I would say: 1

Here's why:

In many countries, including those in North America, employees are entitled to paid time off (PTO) or vacation days as part of their employment benefits. Typically, this is accrued over time, and employees can use it to recharge, relax, and attend to personal matters.

Given that you've been employed for over a year and haven't taken any time off, it's reasonable to assume that you've accumulated some PTO or vacation days. Requesting a vacation now would be a normal and expected use of your accrued benefits.

It's worth noting that some employers may have specific policies or restrictions on taking time off, so it's always a good idea to review your employment contract or speak with HR to understand your company's policies. However, in general, taking a vacation after a year of employment is a common and reasonable request.
